newsitem.title: UK: Support for world sugar prices seen sustained -Man.
newsitem.headline: Support for world sugar prices seen sustained -Man.

text.p: Uncertainty over crops in key producing nations should support world sugar prices despite short-term surpluses and a possible rise in Brazil's exports, trade house E D & F Man said on Monday.
In its latest report, Man said the market had shown little possibility of shifting out of its trapped ranges, a feature reinforced by uncertainty over the coming crops in Thailand, India and Cuba.

The slowdown in the flow of east European surplus tonnages onto the world market had also helped support white sugar prices despite the abundance of stocks in the European Union and elsewhere in central Europe, it said.
"The market has thus coped well with the reports of possible increases in Brazilian shipments," Man said.
"The underlying support for prices is therefore likely to be sustained despite the short-term surpluses and the prospect of mounting pressure on nearby switches," the report added.
Brazil recently increased sugar export quotas to 5.3 million tonnes tel quel from 3.7 million in centre-south growing area and to 1.9 million from 1.6 million in the north-northeast.
Estimates of Brazilian 1997/98 exports were increased to more than six million tonnes after 5.3 million in 1996/97 although total export quotas now stood at 7.2 million, the Man report said.
